 Deadline: Legal Blog 
 Trump nominee worries that saying who won the 2020 election could be an ‘ethical violation’
 If confirmed, Cody Hiland will have a lifetime appointment on a federal court that is one level below the Supreme Court. 
 Play 
 Trump rushes to fill judicial seats before Democrats take over 
 November 13, 2026 / 07:13 
 By  
 Jordan Rubin 
 Nov. 18, 2026, 3:42 PM EST 
 Is it unethical to tell the truth about a publicly known fact?
 President Donald Trump ’s nominee for a federal appeals court seat suggested it could be.
 Cody Hiland ’s suggestion came during his confirmation hearing Wednesday, when Sen. Richard Blumenthal , D-Conn., posed the question that many a Trump nominee before him has likewise refused to answer : Who won the 2020 election?
 BLUMENTHAL: Who won the 2020 election?HILAND: I'm not going to answer thatBLUMENTHAL: Why? H: Because it's going down a political track on an issue that happened 6 years ago, & I don't want to come close to an ethical violationB: We know the White House told you, 'Don't answer that question'
— Aaron Rupar (@atrupar.com) 2026-11-18T17:55:34.425Z 
 Hiland, who is currently a justice on the Arkansas Supreme Court, began by giving what has become a standard nonanswer of saying that Joe Biden was certified as the winner of that election.
 Blumenthal followed up by asking Hiland who won the popular vote (which Biden did, by more than 7 million votes).
 The nominee responded by telling the senator that the popular vote “is not what’s important, respectfully,” adding that he thought the Electoral College was the appropriate answer to the senator’s question (which was not about the Electoral College). Blumenthal observed that he was asking a factual question.

 Jordan Rubin 
 Hiland continued to avoid answering it directly before ultimately calling it a “political” subject that he just wouldn’t answer.
 Blumenthal then asked another simple question — “why?” — to which the nominee responded that he didn’t want to risk a “potential ethical violation.”
 That led the senator to incredulously repeat the nominee’s logic back to him: “An ethical violation in answering a strictly factual question?”
 Blumenthal said the line of questioning was a test of the nominee’s independence.
 Hiland thus became the latest Trump nominee to fail that test. But had he passed, he would have risked getting his nomination pulled by the president who tried to overturn his defeat in that election.
 Jordan Rubin 
 Jordan Rubin is the Deadline: Legal Blog writer. He was a prosecutor for the New York County District Attorney’s Office in Manhattan and is the author of “Bizarro," a book about the secret war on synthetic drugs. Before he joined MS NOW, he was a legal reporter for Bloomberg Law.
